title: Conditional reading in the Gospels
subtitle: State the condition without deciding more than the text says.
overview: Conditions in Gospel discourse often carry invitation, warning, or promise. First identify protasis and conclusion, then read their rhetorical setting.
Avoid treating every ἐάν clause as a mathematical statement about probability or perseverance; grammar supplies structure, context supplies force.

sections.title: Conditional map
rows: you are able to cleanse me

items.grc: ἐὰν ὑμεῖς μείνητε ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τῷ ἐμῷ, ἀληθῶς μαθηταί μού ἐστε.
items.en: If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples.
If you are willing, you are able to cleanse me.
